The report is explicit that it knows the gate fires: its own pivot card records that under the standing protocol this trade would be suppressed on this basis, that suppression is lifted by run instruction, and that the limitation is disclosed on the card instead. That is not available. The suppression triggers are non-discretionary, and no run-time direction, user instruction, operator note or leniency argument may relax, defer or reverse them; a card emitted against a fired gate is a P-level failure however well formed, and the only compliant outputs are the suppressed row or a rebuild that clears the gate on its merits. It is recorded here as arithmetic that was never reached, not as a contingent order: the row carries no entry, no stop, no R and no targets, all of which are null by rule. Order-side, ladder-order, R-band and TP1-distance tests are not applicable to a suppressed row. Linter: SUPPRESSED, zero DUD.
